mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to potential tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn can cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI increases and negative returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased costs for businesses, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between low unemployment and negative returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.3 million units signals strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between high housing starts and positive returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between decreased industrial production and negative returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between increasing nonfarm payrolls and positive returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1), it signals strong consumer demand, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of RSAFS growth outpacing GDPC1 growth on positive returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a contraction in both supply and labor, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of decreasing industrial production and increasing unemployment on negative returns is not statistically significant.
